19509-the-opinions-of-a-philosopher.title: The Opinions Of A Philosopher.
19509-the-opinions-of-a-philosopher.creator: Robert Grant
19509-the-opinions-of-a-philosopher.description: A book by Robert Grant. they are to be found in the peaceful environs of a university or on some mountain top a Sabbath day's journey from the hum of civilization, where they eschew nearly everything which the every-day mortal finds requisite to comfort and convenience, unless it be whiskey and water. I have sometimes fancied that more real philosophers than we are aware of are partial on the sly to whiskey and water.

arxiv-2105-06538.title: Vibratory Powder Feeding for Powder Bed Additive Manufacturing using Water and Gas Atomized Metal Powders
arxiv-2105-06538.creator: C. W. Sinclair, R. Edinger, W. Sparling, A. Molavi-Kakhki, C. Labrecque
arxiv-2105-06538.description: Abstract Commercial powder bed fusion additive manufacturing systems use recoaters for the layer-by-layer distribution of powder. Despite the known limitations of recoaters, there has been relatively little work presented on the possible benefits of alternative powder delivery systems. Here, we show the use of a technology using simple vibration to control the powder flow for powder bed additive manufacturing.

arxiv-2108-04025.title: On differential operators and unifying relations for 1 1 -loop Feynman integrands
arxiv-2108-04025.creator: Kang Zhou
arxiv-2108-04025.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kang Zhou. We generalize the unifying relations for tree amplitudes to the 1 1 -loop Feynman integrands. By employing the 1 1 -loop CHY formula, we construct differential operators which transmute the 1 1 -loop gravitational Feynman integrand to Feynman integrands for a wide range of theories, include Einstein-Yang-Mills theory, Einstein-Maxwell theory, pure Yang-Mills theory, Yang-Mills-scalar theory, Born-Infeld theory, Dirac-Born-Infeld theory, bi-adjoint scalar theory, non-linear sigma model, as well as special Galileon theory. The unified web at 1 1 -loop level is established.

arxiv-2201-04647.title: The Rate, Amplitude and Duration of Outbursts from Class 0 Protostars in Orion
arxiv-2201-04647.creator: Wafa Zakri, S. T. Megeath, William J. Fischer, Robert Gutermuth, Elise Furlan, Lee Hartmann, Nicole Karnath, Mayra Osorio, Emily Safron, Thomas Stanke, Amelia M. Stutz, John J. Tobin, Thomas S. Allen, Sam Federman, Nolan Habel, P. Manoj, Mayank Narang, Riwaj Pokhrel, Luisa Rebull, Patrick D. Sheehan
arxiv-2201-04647.description: Abstract At least half of a protostar’s mass is accreted in the Class 0 phase, when the central protostar is deeply embedded in a dense, infalling envelope. We present the first systematic search for outbursts from Class 0 protostars in the Orion clouds.

arxiv-2206-11956.title: Word maps with constants on symmetric groups
arxiv-2206-11956.creator: Jakob Schneider, Andreas Thom
arxiv-2206-11956.description: Abstract . We study word maps with constants on symmetric groups. Even though there are non-trivial mixed identities of bounded length that are valid for all symmetric groups, we show that no such identities can hold in the limit in a metric sense.

arxiv-2208-06507.title: Continual Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation using a Class-Specific Transfer Thanks: This publication was created as part of the research project ”KI Delta Learning” (project number: 19A19013R) funded by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWi) on the basis o
arxiv-2208-06507.creator: Robert A. Marsden, Felix Wiewel, Mario Döbler, Yang Yang and Bin Yang
arxiv-2208-06507.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Robert A. Marsden, Felix Wiewel, Mario Döbler, Yang Yang and Bin Yang. In recent years, there has been tremendous progress in the field of semantic image segmentation. However, one remaining challenging problem is that segmentation models do not generalize to unseen domains. To overcome this problem, one either has to label lots of data covering the whole variety of possible domains, which is often infeasible in practice, or apply unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA), only requiring labeled source data.

arxiv-2411-02165.title: Joint Training of Speaker Embedding Extractor, Speech and Overlap Detection for Diarization Thanks: Computing on IT4I supercomputer was supported by the Czech Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports through the e-INFRA CZ (ID:90254).
arxiv-2411-02165.creator: Petr Pálka 1 , Federico Landini 1 , Dominik Klement 1 , Mireia Diez 1 , Anna Silnova 1 , Marc Delcroix 2 , Lukáš Burget 1
arxiv-2411-02165.description: Abstract In spite of the popularity of end-to-end diarization systems nowadays, modular systems comprised of voice activity detection (VAD), speaker embedding extraction plus clustering, and overlapped speech detection (OSD) plus handling still attain competitive performance in many conditions. However, one of the main drawbacks of modular systems is the need to run (and train) different modules independently.

arxiv-2412-13425.title: A note on the frequency gaps between integers in the thin obstacle problem
arxiv-2412-13425.creator: Federico Franceschini, Ovidiu Savin
arxiv-2412-13425.description: Abstract . We give a simple proof of the fact that — in all dimensions — there are no homogeneous solutions to the thin obstacle problem with frequency λ \lambda belonging to intervals of the form ( 2 ​ k , 2 ​ k + 1 ) (2k,2k+1) , k ∈ ℕ k\in\mathbb{N} .

arxiv-2502-02649.title: Fully Autonomous AI Agents Should Not be Developed
arxiv-2502-02649.creator: Margaret Mitchell, Avijit Ghosh, Alexandra Sasha Luccioni, Giada Pistilli
arxiv-2502-02649.description: Abstract We argue that fully autonomous AI agents should not be developed . In support of this position, we build from prior scientific literature and current product marketing to detail the ethical values at play in the use of AI agents, documenting trade-offs in potential benefits and risks.

arxiv-2502-09767.title: Non-Markovian Discrete Diffusion with Causal Language Models
arxiv-2502-09767.creator: Yangtian Zhang, Sizhuang He, Daniel Levine, Lawrence Zhao, David Zhang, Shiyang Zhang, Emanuele Zappala, Rex Ying, David van Dijk, emanuele.zappala@isu.edu
arxiv-2502-09767.description: Abstract Discrete diffusion models offer a flexible, controllable approach to structured sequence generation, yet they still lag behind causal language models in expressive power. A key limitation lies in their reliance on the Markovian assumption, which restricts each step to condition only on the current state, leading to potential uncorrectable error accumulation.

arxiv-2506-14620.title: Differential Privacy and Survey Sampling
arxiv-2506-14620.creator: Daniel Bonnéry, Julien Jamme
arxiv-2506-14620.description: Abstract The Horvitz-Thompson estimate of a total can be seen as as differentially private mechanism applied to this population total. We provide forumlae to compute the ϵ \epsilon and δ \delta parameter for this specific mecanism, coupled or not coupled with the addition of a Laplace or a Gaussian noise.

arxiv-2511-23275.title: Conjugate Generalised Bayesian Inference for Discrete Doubly Intractable Problems
arxiv-2511-23275.creator: William Laplante †1,2,4 , Matias Altamirano 2 , Jeremias Knoblauch 2 , Andrew Duncan 3 , and François-Xavier Briol 2
arxiv-2511-23275.description: Abstract Doubly intractable problems occur when both the likelihood and the posterior are available only in unnormalised form, with computationally intractable normalisation constants. Bayesian inference then typically requires direct approximation of the posterior through specialised and typically expensive MCMC methods.

arxiv-2601-19384.title: GenPairX: A Hardware-Algorithm Co-Designed Accelerator for Paired-End Read Mapping
arxiv-2601-19384.creator: Julien Eudine † \dagger Chu Li † \dagger Zhuo Cheng † \dagger Renzo Andri † \dagger Can Firtina ‡ \ddagger Mohammad Sadrosadati ‡ \ddagger Nika Mansouri Ghiasi ‡ \ddagger Konstantina Koliogeorgi ‡ \ddagger Anirban Nag † \dagger Arash Tavakkol † \dagger Haiyu Mao ¶ \mathparagraph Onur Mutlu ‡ \ddagge
arxiv-2601-19384.description: Abstract Genome sequencing has become a central focus in computational biology due to its critical role in applications such as personalized medicine, disease outbreak tracking, and evolutionary research. A genome study typically begins with sequencing, which produces millions to billions of short DNA fragments known as reads.

pmc-10576761.title: Miniature spatial transcriptomics for studying parasite-endosymbiont relationships at the micro scale
pmc-10576761.creator: Hailey Sounart, Denis Voronin, Yuvarani Masarapu, Matthew Chung, Sami Saarenpää, Elodie Ghedin, Stefania Giacomello
pmc-10576761.description: Several important human infectious diseases are caused by microscale-sized parasitic nematodes like filarial worms. Filarial worms have their own spatial tissue organization; to uncover this tissue structure, we need methods that can spatially resolve these miniature specimens. Most filarial worms evolved a mutualistic association with endosymbiotic bacteria Wolbachia.

pmc-10853352.title: Handwriting but not typewriting leads to widespread brain connectivity: a high-density EEG study with implications for the classroom
pmc-10853352.creator: F. R. (Ruud) Van der Weel, Audrey L. H. Van der Meer
pmc-10853352.description: As traditional handwriting is progressively being replaced by digital devices, it is essential to investigate the implications for the human brain. Brain electrical activity was recorded in 36 university students as they were handwriting visually presented words using a digital pen and typewriting the words on a keyboard.

pmc-11658259.title: Risk factors for anxiety, depression, stress, and their comorbidities among nurses: a prospective cohort from 2020 to 2022
pmc-11658259.creator: Xiaomei Hu, Wenbi Mu, Jing Zhou, Hang Zhou, Xiaokai Yan, Kunyan Yue, TongLing Liu, Wenbi Huang, Liping Ren, Fengming Zou, Anyan Zhang, Xia Sun, Hui Zeng
pmc-11658259.description: BackgroundNurses are at the forefront of healthcare delivery during the COVID-19, placing them at an increased risk for mental health issues. This study aimed to identify the risk factors for anxiety, depression, stress, and their comorbidities among nurses during the 2020–2022 period.MethodsA prospective cohort of nurses in Zunyi City, China, was followed from 2020 to 2022.

pmc-11920965.title: The Central Roles of Keratinocytes in Coordinating Skin Immunity
pmc-11920965.creator: Jared Simmons, Richard L. Gallo
pmc-11920965.description: The function of keratinocytes (KCs) to form a barrier and produce cytokines is well-known, but recent progress has revealed many different roles for KCs in regulation of skin immunity. In this review, we provide an update on the current understanding of how KCs communicate with microbes, immunocytes, neurons, and other cells to form an effective immune barrier.

pmc-12582452.title: Evaluation of the novel HEalthy Lifestyle Project (HELP) youth mental health e-intervention for lifestyle behaviour change and mental healthcare system impact: A randomized controlled trial protocol
pmc-12582452.creator: Ria Patel, Patricia E. Longmuir, Marjorie Robb, Natasha Baechler, Kimberly Courtney, Mark Norris, Gary Goldfield, Fiona Cooligan, Shannon Watson, Paula Cloutier, Clare Gray
pmc-12582452.description: BackgroundYouth mental health is in crisis: suicide and self-harm doubled from 2019–2022; youth wait 8–12 months for care; 75% of youth with mental illness do not get care. Sleep, physical activity, and screen time impact mental wellbeing; lifestyle factors addressed with 95% of youth receiving mental health care.

pmc-12599153.title: Stochastic resonance stimulation effect on stability during walking in people with Parkinson disease
pmc-12599153.creator: Eman Alsaqabi, Stephen DiBianca, Ashwini Sansare, Khushboo Verma, Hendrik Reimann, John Jeka
pmc-12599153.description: People with Parkinson disease (PwPD) often face challenges with maintaining balance while walking, which can stem from sensory dysfunction. Studies have identified different biomechanical strategies that aid in preserving upright balance control. Stochastic resonance (SR) stimulation delivers sub-threshold electrical noise to enhance the detection capabilities of dysfunctional sensory systems.

pmc-12757302.title: Recent advances and evolving strategies in the treatment of lumbar disc herniation
pmc-12757302.creator: Yun Tong, Lanying Yu, Kaifeng Luo, Xiong Yan, Ming Chen, Libin Wang
pmc-12757302.description: Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) remains a leading cause of low back pain and sciatica, imposing a considerable global health and socioeconomic burden. Over the past decades, substantial progress has been made in both conservative and surgical interventions, yet controversies persist regarding optimal treatment strategies, long-term efficacy, and recurrence prevention.

pmc-12778730.title: A Novel Case of Transverse Sinus Stenting and Ticagrelor Use During Pregnancy for Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension
pmc-12778730.creator: Mayur S. Patel, Asad S. Akhter, Matthew T. Rocco, Abdussamad Akhter, Shahid M. Nimjee
pmc-12778730.description: BackgroundIdiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is prevalent among the US population, with exacerbation of symptoms during pregnancy. Transverse sinus stenting is a new effective treatment for IIH. Stenting is avoided in pregnancy largely due to the requirement of dual antiplatelet therapy.

pmc-12827599.title: Two virulent bacteriophages targeting carbapenem-resistant Raoultella planticola
pmc-12827599.creator: Cuong V. Hoang, Jonathan Fan, Lauren Bhasin, Anthony Del Mundo, Vanessa Law, Dominic Nguyen, Suraj Ganiger, Ashley Mansour, Christi L. McElheny, Yohei Doi, Olakunle I. Olawole

Carbapenem-resistant Raoultella planticola (CRRP) is an emerging nosocomial pathogen with limited therapeutic options. Here, we describe the comparative characterization of two novel virulent bacteriophages, Macy and Sally, both isolated from the same soil microenvironment. Macy exhibits exceptional lytic potency, with a burst size of 8,375 PFU per infected cell, narrow host specificity, and pronounced biofilm-disrupting activity likely mediated by a putative depolymerase. In contrast, Sally displays a broader host range, infecting both R.

pmc-13194432.title: Use of axillary vascular grafts in prophylactic lymphovenous bypass: technical challenges and lessons learned
pmc-13194432.creator: Jorge Flores Garcia, J. Michael Smith, Ramin Rajaii, Emily L. Geisler, Roman J. Skoracki, Min-Jeong Cho
pmc-13194432.description: BackgroundBreast cancer–related lymphedema (BCRL) is a common and debilitating complication of axillary lymph node dissection (ALND), affecting approximately 1 in 5 patients. While preventive lymphatic surgeries such as prophylactic lymphovenous bypass (pLVB) performed at the time of ALND have been shown to decrease the risk of developing BCRL, success is frequently limited by inadequate recipient veins within the axilla.

pmc-13224272.title: Internal carotid artery agenesis: A narrative review
pmc-13224272.creator: Khalid Talal Alghamdi, Badr E. Hafiz, Zubaidah Alahmari, Thamer H. Alsharif, Homoud Aldahash, Saleh S. Baeesa
pmc-13224272.description: Background: Congenital anomalies of the internal carotid artery (ICA), including hypoplasia, aplasia, and agenesis, are rare vascular conditions with a prevalence below 0.01%. Most patients remain asymptomatic because of collateral cerebral circulation, yet these anomalies may cause cerebrovascular complications, particularly ischemic events and intracranial aneurysm formation.

pmc-13368770.creator: Sai Spoorthy Mamidipalli, Lakshmi Sristi, Barikar C. Malathesh, Sai Krishna Tikka, Madhavi Eerike

pmc-6323917.creator: Kozomara A, Birgaoanu M, Griffiths-Jones S.
pmc-6323917.description: Peer-reviewed research article (PubMed Central). miRBase catalogs, names and distributes microRNA gene sequences.
